summary:
ORBITAL X is an AI-powered scientific intelligence platform designed to help researchers understand fire behaviour in microgravity and improve spacecraft fire safety.

On Earth, gravity influences flame behaviour through natural convection. However, in microgravity, flames behave differently, affecting heat transfer, oxygen transport and combustion patterns. This creates unique challenges for detecting and managing fire aboard spacecraft.

ORBITAL X addresses this challenge by integrating accessible NASA combustion research and experimental datasets into a unified platform. It provides interactive data visualizations, temperature trend analysis, Earth-versus-microgravity comparisons and AI/ML-powered pattern and anomaly detection. The platform also generates evidence-based research insights that connect scientific observations to potential fire detection, thermal monitoring and suppression strategies.

By simplifying access to complex scientific data and supporting intelligent analysis, ORBITAL X aims to assist aerospace researchers, combustion scientists and spacecraft engineers in developing safer fire-safety strategies for future space missions.
details:
Project Name: ORBITAL X – Flame Intelligence | Microgravity Fire Safety Platform

ORBITAL X is a scientific data analysis and fire-safety research platform designed to help researchers and aerospace engineers better understand how flames behave in microgravity environments. Fire behaves differently in space because gravity-driven convection is greatly reduced, which can affect flame shape, heat transfer, oxygen transport, and combustion behaviour. These differences create unique fire-safety challenges for astronauts and spacecraft.

Our platform brings relevant NASA microgravity combustion research data into one accessible interface. It allows users to explore available experiments, visualize scientific measurements through interactive graphs, compare compatible combustion observations, and use AI-assisted analytical methods to identify patterns, trends, and unusual behaviour in the data. It also aims to translate scientific findings into understandable, evidence-linked fire-safety research insights.

The major benefit of ORBITAL X is that it reduces the difficulty of finding, understanding, and analysing complex scientific datasets. Instead of manually exploring multiple research sources and interpreting raw measurements, users can access relevant information through a centralized platform. This can support researchers in studying flame behaviour, identifying research gaps, and exploring better approaches to spacecraft fire detection, monitoring, and prevention.

The intended impact is to contribute to safer future space missions by making microgravity combustion research more accessible and useful. The platform can support aerospace researchers, students, combustion scientists, and spacecraft safety engineers in making more informed research decisions. ORBITAL X is designed as a research-support tool and does not replace physical experiments or certified spacecraft safety systems.

Technology and Tools:

  • Frontend: React, TypeScript, HTML, CSS, and Tailwind CSS.
  • Backend: Python and FastAPI.
  • Data analysis: Pandas, NumPy, and Scikit-learn.
  • Data visualization: Recharts or Plotly.
  • Data sources: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) and NASA FIRMS, where relevant and accessible.
  • Database: PostgreSQL or SQLite.
  • AI-assisted analysis: Machine-learning methods for pattern identification, comparison, and anomaly detection.

Creativity and Innovation:

The creative aspect of ORBITAL X is its approach of connecting scientific research, data visualization, and AI-assisted interpretation in one platform. Rather than simply displaying research papers or raw datasets, it aims to help users explore the relationship between gravity conditions and combustion behaviour. Its key concept is the Gravity Intelligence Engine, which helps users examine available experimental data, compare relevant observations, and understand how combustion characteristics may change under different gravity conditions.

Factors Considered:

While developing the concept, our team considered astronaut safety, the limitations of conducting experiments in space, the complexity of scientific datasets, data accuracy, accessibility, and the reliability of AI-generated interpretations. We also considered the importance of distinguishing actual NASA experimental observations from model predictions and simulations. Every scientific insight should be traceable to its source, and the platform should clearly communicate uncertainty and limitations.

Through ORBITAL X, our goal is to turn complex microgravity combustion research into accessible scientific intelligence that can contribute to the development of safer space environments.
